system.summary: The State Department's numerical syllable-and-word code (the JQA table, the = 1385, about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa), in Morris's copy with its sixteen blocks of 100 numbered in reverse order: Morris 100*i + r = JQA 100*(15 - i) + r, each block keeping its inner order (the = 285, of = 76).
system.sibling_key: the JQA code, ../jqa/code_table.tsv (rebuilt there from the State Department clerk's decodes and Ford's printed decipherments of JQA's 1811-1812 despatches), applied unchanged under the block order in block_map.tsv
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct numbers in morris1813_transcription.txt (decode.py). Groups are joined by dots within a word and separated by a space between words. Marks under groups (5, 55, 5555, c, s) and a short double stroke after groups are transcribed; their meaning is not known. 361 and 364 (= JQA 1261, 1264) behave as comma and full stop, as in the Ellis 1839 alignment (open PR #107). From PR #200 on the readings use a surviving sheet of the code itself (beling/key/codebook_M97_13_transcription.csv, NARA M97 roll 13, Weber's WE028) instead of the table rebuilt in ../jqa. Marks: a hook under a group doubles a letter, strokes under it withdraw letters, an angle after it marks a plural or ending (mark rules of PR #200). The Cevallos note of 20 November 1814 is Spanish spelled with this English code.

prior_solution.where: Clerks' decipherments on other copies: No. 24 (frame 0196), No. 25 (frame 0174), the Cevallos note (frames 0169-0170), and by the catalogue's vetting the letter of 24 March 1815 (frames 0206-0207, not compared). None on the frames of Nos. 17, 18, 19 and 28 or on frame 0039, whose text has clear copies (M37 roll 2 frames 395-396; M31 roll 14 frames 0059-0060). H. L. Dufour Woolfley, A Quaker Goes to Spain (2013), quotes coded passages of 4 and 11 April 1814 (Ebook Central p. 78) and parts of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 (pp. 98-99, 100, 106); all found after the readings; the page references were not checked at integration. W. R. Manning (1925) vol. 3 searched: none found. Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 searched by Google Books snippets only (catalogue vetting, 3 Nov 2026: 20 September 1814 and 12 May 1815 not printed there as far as snippets show). American State Papers, Foreign Relations, not searched beyond two web searches on 12 Nov 2026. The Anthony Morris Family Papers at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania (2018-A) not seen. Claiborne's three letters (claiborne/): Jacob Wagner's decipherments stand between the lines and are printed in the Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State series, with the note 'State Department code; key not found' (by the contributor's record and search snippets; Founders Online was not opened); known before the work and used as the plaintext.

solution.what: WAINUT contribution: NARA M31 roll 14 frames 0036-0039 fetched; frame 0039 (page '4', code with clear phrases in lines 1-6) chosen to work on.
WAINUT contribution: frame 0039 transcribed from the full frame and enlarged crops, lines 1-6 and 10-12 first, then lines 7-9 and 13-26: 554 groups in 26 lines.

WAINUT contribution: 220 number-to-value tables from the repository (main and open WAINUT pull requests) applied directly to the groups and scored on function words: none fits (best function-word share 0.11).

WAINUT contribution: constant shifts of the group numbers, with and without a modulus, against the US tables: the JQA table at +1100 stands out (function-word share 0.25 against 0.03 for the next tables) because one block of 100 lines up.

WAINUT contribution: best JQA offset for each Morris block of 100: the busy blocks give +1500, +1300, +1100 (Morris 1-300), which suggests the sixteen blocks in reverse order (block_map.tsv); the first round overstated this as a clean pattern in every block. On the corrected transcription function words alone pick that block for 8 of 16 Morris blocks (1-300, 401-500, 601-700, 801-1100); the other eight follow from the pattern and from context.

WAINUT contribution: a second agent re-read 144 groups blind from the image (140 agree) and re-applied the method with its own code. The three clear misreadings it found (L9 724 -> 721 dem, L9 131 -> 13 ad, L24 108 -> 608 or) each turn a broken syllable into the expected one (democratic, administration, ambassador). It corrected overstated counts of the first round: 76.285 'of the' 15x (not 25x); 'territory' and 'insurrection' 2x each as identical group strings (not 3x).

WAINUT contribution: decode.py --controls on the 552 groups: block_map.tsv coverage 0.917, function words 0.353; identity 0.630 / 0.058; 20,000 random orders of the 16 blocks: function words median 0.062, 99.9th percentile 0.250, max 0.297. Per block, against word bigrams of Ford, Writings of JQA vols 3-4, the block_map.tsv block ranks first (one tie) for 15 of 16 Morris blocks; Morris 1501-1600 ranks second (3 bigrams against 4) and is kept from the pattern and from context (should, United States, Minister).

WAINUT contribution: frame 0039 written out as sentences (morris1813_reading.md): 506 of 554 groups have a table value; read_share 0.678 (research/reading_audit/v2_score.py hole rate 0.322); 670 read [?Floridas] from context at all five occurrences; names Jefferson, Madison, Baton Rouge from the table syllables.

WAINUT contribution: one web search and two by the verifier found no printed decipherment and no record of the code with reversed blocks. Manning (1925) vol. 3, Woolfley and the HSP Morris papers not checked.

Andrew Beling, with AI agents: 68 frames of M31 roll 14 fetched around the coded frames catalogue 650 left open; the copies identified as Nos. 18, 19, 24, 25 and 28 (frame 0139 is the coded part of No. 19, not of No. 18); a wholly coded document on 0115-0116 and three coded lines on 0111 found and not read.

Words that the groups do not give were marked as inferences where they were not: 'liberal' and 'liberality' (li-er-al) in No. 18, 'approbation' (ap-pro-bat-ad) in No. 19. All letters recounted by one rule (word_share.py): 0.972, 0.946, 0.962, 0.958, 0.943, 0.977, 1.000, 0.957, 0.977, 1.000. No. 19 and No. 13 fall under 0.95. In No. 24 the opening 593.813 is compared with 598.813 = Sir at the head of 24 March 1815.

The contributor's follow-up commit c84e484c to PR 415, after the integration: his own reading reviews (grade A) of the five catalogue 650 letters, 'actu[al]' marked as supplied in No. 28, 'office' noted as read by the stroke rule in No. 19, and the opening 593.813 of No. 24 left as numbers. Checked against the files: No. 28 now has one hole in 71 coded words (0.986, was 1.000), so the thirteen texts have 87 holes in 2,631 words (0.967); the earlier profile figure of 85 holes and the 96.8% in the ledgers did not match the NOTES recount (86 before this commit) and are corrected to 87 and 96.7%. texts.label: Morris to Monroe, Cadiz, 4 January 1814 and enclosed proposal, M31 roll 14 frame 0039 (page '4'), catalogue 650

reading_review.note: Read as sentences: coherent with scattered holes. The page starts and ends mid-sentence, and the digit rereads behind it were made by agents with the clear text in view (beling/frame39/frame0039_rereads.md).

texts.summary: The end of Morris's cover letter of 4 January 1814, signed in code: the US should keep a force near Florida against the British, and a change in the Regency would help them. Then the start of the proposal he enclosed, whose allegations are its author's: that Jefferson and Madison worked to separate Spain's American colonies, instigated the West Florida insurrection, seized Baton Rouge and encouraged the revolutionaries of Caracas.

texts.summary: East Florida might be bought on moderate terms, partly paid in produce of the United States, but only with presents or douceurs of perhaps ten thousand dollars; Morris is still waiting at Cadiz for a reply to his proposal.
